chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his ancestors (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'My Ummah will remain in goodness as long as they do not betray one another, fulfill the trust, and pay the Zakat. And when they do not do that, they will be tested with drought and years of hardship.'
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a community to remain in goodness according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of the Ahl al-Bayt in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A’mal*, links communal spiritual integrity to material prosperity, emphasizing that internal cohesion and fiscal justice (Zakat) are prerequisites for divine favor. The mention of 'Qahat' (drought) and 'Sinin' (years of famine) reflects the Shia exegetical view that neglecting social trusts invites specific natural calamities as divine corrective measures.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.) narrates from his ancestors that the Holy Prophet (s.a.w.s.) said, “My Ummah will remain safe till they do not betray trust and return the things to their owners and pay Zakat. When they cease to do so, they will face famine and drought.”
